items.title: Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request
Proposed Withdrawal Extension and Opportunity for Public Meeting for the Sugarloaf Petroglyphs and Pine Spring Archeological Sites, Wyoming

data.abstract: The Secretary of the Interior proposes to extend Public Land Order (PLO) No. 6650, as extended by PLO No. 7678, for an additional 20-year term. PLO No. 6650, as extended, withdrew 20 acres of public lands, subject to valid existing rights, from settlement, sale, location, or entry under the general land laws, including the United States mining laws, but not from leasing under the mineral leasing laws, to protect the educational, scientific, and artistic values as well as the capital investment for Sugarloaf Petroglyphs and Pine Spring Archeological Sites in Sweetwater County, Wyoming. This Notice advises the public of an opportunity to comment on the proposed withdrawal extension and to request a public meeting.

items.title: Request for Comments Concerning Proposed Modification of Section 301 Action on Brazil's Acts, Policies, and Practices Related to Digital Trade and Electronic Payment Services; Unfair, Preferential Tariffs; Anti-Corruption Enforcement; Intellectual Property Protection; Ethanol Market Access; and Illegal Deforestation
tags: Trade Representative, Office of United States

agencies: Trade Representative, Office of United States
data.abstract: The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) proposes a modification of the tariff action taken in connection with the Section 301 investigation of Brazil's acts, policies, and practices related to digital trade and electronic payment services; unfair, preferential tariffs; anti-corruption enforcement; intellectual property protection; ethanol market access; and illegal deforestation. Brazil has made insufficient progress in eliminating the acts, policies, and practices USTR identified as actionable. The proposed modification to duties on certain sugar products and finished aircraft seeks to create additional leverage to encourage Brazil to eliminate its acts, policies, and practices identified as actionable in the investigation. USTR is seeking public comment and will hold a public hearing regarding this proposed modification.

items.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With a Section 4(d) Rule for Blanding's Turtle

data.abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Blanding's turtle (Emydoidea blandingii), a reptile species from 14 States in the midwestern and eastern regions of the United States and 3 Provinces in eastern Canada, as a threatened species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Blanding's turtle. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not prudent.

Truth in Lending (Regulation Z)

data.abstract: The Board and the Bureau (collectively, Agencies) are publishing final rules amending the official interpretations for the Agencies' regulations that implement the Truth in Lending Act (TILA). The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Dodd- Frank Act) amended TILA to require that the dollar threshold for exempt consumer credit transactions be adjusted annually by the annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the annual percentage increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $73,400 to $76,300 effective January 1, 2027. Because the Dodd- Frank Act also requires similar adjustments in the Consumer Leasing Act's threshold for exempt consumer leases, the Agencies are making similar amendments to each of their respective regulations implementing the Consumer Leasing Act elsewhere in the Rules section of this issue of the Federal Register.

items.title: Consumer Leasing (Regulation M)

data.abstract: The Board and the Bureau (collectively, Agencies) are finalizing amendments to the official interpretations for the Agencies' regulations that implement the Consumer Leasing Act (CLA). The Dodd- Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Dodd-Frank Act) amended the CLA to require that the dollar threshold for exempt consumer leases be adjusted annually by the annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the annual percentage increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $73,400 to $76,300, effective January 1, 2027. Because the Dodd-Frank Act also requires similar adjustments in the Truth in Lending Act's threshold for exempt consumer credit transactions, the Agencies are making similar amendments to each of their respective regulations implementing the Truth in Lending Act elsewhere in the Rules section of this issue of the Federal Register.

items.title: Appraisals for Higher-Priced Mortgage Loans Exemption Threshold

data.abstract: The OCC, the Board, and the Bureau are finalizing amendments to the official interpretations for their regulations that implement section 129H of the Truth in Lending Act (TILA). Section 129H of TILA establishes special appraisal requirements for "higher-risk mortgages," termed "higher-priced mortgage loans" or "HPMLs" in the agencies' regulations. The regulations provide that transactions of $25,000 or less are exempt from these requirements, adjusted annually based on any annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the CPI-W in effect as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $34,200 to $35,500, effective January 1, 2027.

items.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status for Streaked Horned Lark With a Section 4(d) Rule

data.abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the streaked horned lark (Eremophila alpestris strigata), a subspecies of grassland songbird from Oregon and Washington, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would maintain the species as a threatened species on the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and continue to extend the Act's protections to the species.
